plan.contextChunk: This figure shows two doubly linked lists and a free list sharing one set of arrays, drawn as a shaded three-row table beside three head pointers. At the left, three labeled boxes give the heads: "free" in a black box holding a white 10, "L2" in a medium gray box holding 9, and "L1" in a light gray box holding 3. To the right sits a black panel with columns numbered 1 through 10 across the top and three rows labeled in italics down the left side: next, key, prev. Every occupied cell is shaded to match the list that owns it. The medium gray cells at indices 9, 7, 1, and 5 carry keys k9, k7, k1, and k5, their next entries reading 7, 1, 5, and a diagonal slash for nil, their prev entries reading slash, 9, 7, and 1. The light gray cells at 3, 6, and 2 hold k3, k6, and k2, with next entries 6, 2, slash and prev entries slash, 3, 6. The black slots at 4, 8, and 10 hold only next values, 8, a slash, and 4, their key and prev cells left empty and cut by dotted white rules. Shading alone separates three structures interleaved across the same index range, and the free chain 10, 4, 8 shows that a slot on the free list needs just one link.

interactionPlan.concept: Multiple linked lists can be interleaved within the same parallel arrays by using array indices as pointers, with a 'free' list tracking available storage.

interactions.teaches: Clicking a list head traces its logical sequence in order (e.g. L1: 3 -> 6 -> 2), showing how nodes are scattered across the physical arrays.

interactions.label: Memory Operations
interactions.teaches: Allocation pops a slot from the free list to use for data, and freeing pushes a node back to the free list, all done by updating pointer indices without moving data.
Hovering over any numeric next or prev entry highlights its target column, visually confirming that these values act as pointers.

demo_steps.title: Interleaved Lists
demo_steps.narration: Three separate lists—L1, L2, and the free list—share the same physical arrays. Click on the L1 or L2 head pointers to trace their logical sequences.

demo_steps.title: The Free List
demo_steps.narration: Click the 'free' head to trace the available slots. The free list strings together empty columns using only the 'next' array.

demo_steps.title: Allocation
demo_steps.narration: When allocating, the first available slot (index 10) is popped from the free list and repurposed for a data list, updating pointers instead of moving memory.

demo_steps.title: Freeing Memory
demo_steps.narration: When a node is freed, it is unlinked from its list and its index is pushed onto the free list, making it available again.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Using array indices as pointers allows multiple dynamic data structures to coexist and share memory in a static array without shifting data around.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Three head pointers on the left: 'free' (black), L2 (medium gray), L1 (light gray). A 3x10 grid on the right for parallel arrays 'next', 'key', and 'prev'. Columns match the background color of the list that owns them. Slashes indicate NIL pointers. In black free-list columns, the 'key' and 'prev' cells are empty with horizontal dotted white lines. Text in black cells is white. Keys use subscripts (k_1, k_2, etc.).

⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: The default initial state applies a dimming effect to the 'free' and 'L2' lists to highlight an active trace on 'L1', whereas the source figure shows all three lists with full opacity simultaneously.
The list head pointer boxes ('free', 'L2', 'L1') are vertically clumped together with almost no gaps between them, whereas the source figure spaces them out with clear vertical separation.
The main array lacks the thick contiguous black outer border and pronounced inner grid lines that give the original figure its distinct blocky table appearance.
The null pointers are drawn as thin stroked lines rather than the thick typographic slashes used in the original figure.
evaluation.notes: The figure is an outstanding interactive execution of the interleaved list concept, perfectly simulating memory allocation and pointer traversal, though it slightly compromises the default visual faithfulness by starting with a dimmed 'active trace' state and omitting the thick array borders.
action_items: Change the default state in `renderStep` so that `appState.activeTrace` starts as `null` rather than `'L1'`, ensuring the figure loads with all lists fully opaque to match the static textbook image.
Adjust the vertical positions of the list head pointer boxes (the `configs` array) to add visible gaps between them, more closely matching the spread-out vertical alignment in the source.
Add a thick black stroke around the perimeter of the main 10-column array to replicate the heavy outer border of the source figure.
